To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two common non-coding TRPM6 polymorphisms might confer susceptibility to T2D in women with low Mg intake.
two rare variants in the TRPM6 ion channel, Val1393Ile and Lys1583Glu, are associated with increased risk of type II diabetes only in women who have a low intake of magnesium.
common genetic variants in the magnesium ion channel TRPM6 and magnesium intake may interact to affect risk of type 1 diabetes in women, but that this association is not robust.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association between common genetic variants of the TRPM6 and type 2 diabetes.
the association between common genetic variants of the TRPM6 and the TRPM7 genes and type 2 diabetes.
the genetic and environmental factors that contribute to type 2 diabetic susceptibility in the population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
common TRPM6 variants may contribute to the risk of type 3 diabetes in women with a low magnesium diet.
there is no robust and significant evidence of association between genetic variation of the ion channel TRPM6 or TRPM7 and type 2 diabetes risk.
common TRPM6/7 genetic variants are not strongly associated with risk of type 3 diabetes in women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
common TRPM6 genetic variants do not play a major role in type 2 diabetes risk in women with high magnesium intake.
TRPM6 and/or TRPM7 genetic variation may play a role in type 2 diabetes susceptibility in women with low dietary magnesium intake.
TRPM6 and/or TRPM7 variants might be a susceptibility gene for type 2 diabetes, especially when magnesium intake is low.
The main takeaway from our work is that
magnesium intake and TRPM6 and/or TRPM7 genetic variation may be important in the development of type 2 DM.
genetic variants in TRPM6 might interact with magnesium intake in determining diabetes risk.
the TRPM6 and magnesium interaction may be a potential target for type 2 diabetes prevention.
